2026-10-05T15:13:00Z_CORRECTION_cloudwat.headline: The longest upstream_ok:false instance since #5581/#5583 deployed (15:11:24Z-15:13:16Z, ~1m52s) just DEFINITIVELY CONFIRMED PR #5583's fix is working in production -- but only after discovering my own CloudWatch search queries all week had a SYNTAX BUG that made every prior 'zero matches, inconclusive' result a FALSE NEGATIVE, not genuine absence.
2026-10-05T15:13:00Z_CORRECTION_cloudwat.the_bug: Every CloudWatch filter_log_events call I made this week (2026-10-02 17:46Z, 19:10-19:11Z instances, and this one's first attempt) used the pattern '"zerodte-ledger-read" OR "zerodte-board-fallback" OR "zerodte-scan"' -- using the literal word OR as a boolean operator, the way you'd write it in SQL or a search engine. CloudWatch Logs filter-pattern syntax does NOT support bare OR between quoted terms -- the correct multi-term-OR syntax is '?term1 ?term2 ?term3' (each ?-prefixed term independently matched, logically ORed). My OR-based pattern silently matched ZERO events every single time, with no error -- it degraded to either a literal-string match (requiring the exact substring '" OR "' inside a log line, which never exists) or some other degenerate no-op, rather than failing loudly. Verified directly this cycle: the bare single-term pattern '"zerodte-board-fallback"' returned 10 matches in the SAME window where my OR-pattern had just returned 0 two minutes earlier.
2026-10-05T15:13:00Z_CORRECTION_cloudwat.corrected_result_this_instance: With the correct syntax, checked all three known tags individually in the 15:10-15:15Z window bracketing this instance: [zerodte-board-fallback] fired 10 times (every log line reads: 'cold build still running past maxBlockMs=3000ms with no Redis snapshot or local last-good board to serve'), [zerodte-ledger-read] 0 matches (correctly -- this instance's root cause is the OTHER route), [zerodte-scan] 10 matches but all were ROUTINE operational lines (market_state/discovery rail mix), not the error path -- confirmed by a direct check for the literal error text 'primary flow fetch failed': 0 matches. So this instance's root cause is cleanly, unambiguously PR #5583's cold-build-timeout route, and PR #5583's fix is now PROVEN working in production with direct log evidence, not just 'merged and deployed, unverified.'
2026-10-05T15:13:00Z_CORRECTION_cloudwat.what_this_means_for_prior_entries: The 2026-10-02 17:46Z and 19:10-19:11Z 'inconclusive, too brief to rule out delivery lag' entries were reasoned about the WRONG variable -- the issue was never instance duration vs. log delivery lag, it was that my search could never have found a match regardless of duration, because the query itself was broken. Those two instances remain genuinely UNATTRIBUTED (never re-queried with the corrected syntax, and the underlying raw log data may or may not still be within CloudWatch's retention window to re-check), but the conclusion they supported -- 'not yet enough evidence either way' -- was accidentally still the right posture to hold, for the wrong reason. The real lesson: a 'zero matches' CloudWatch result is not self-verifying -- ALWAYS sanity-check a zero-match query result against a single bare term that is known/expected to exist, the way this cycle did only after noticing the broad-pattern search surfaced matches the narrow one missed. Apply this check before trusting any future zero-match CloudWatch result in this investigation.
